verdict.winner: Architectural shingles win on durability and wind class; 3-tab shingles win on upfront NJ cost.
verdict.reasoning: Architectural shingles over 3-tab shingles when the roof faces northern-NJ design wind — the 110-130 mph architectural wind warranty meets or exceeds the ~110-115 mph ASCE 7-16 design wind speed mapped for Essex County, while entry 3-tab's ~60 mph warranty falls short.
verdict.alternate: 3-tab shingles win when upfront budget leads the decision — 3-tab installs at $5.50-$9.50 per NJ square foot versus architectural's $6.50-$11.00 (Josten Roofing), the lowest-cost asphalt path for rentals, budget jobs, and code-minimum re-roofs.

keyFacts: Architectural shingles last 30 years versus 20 years for 3-tab shingles (InterNACHI life-expectancy chart).
Architectural shingles install at $6.50-$11.00 per NJ square foot versus $5.50-$9.50 for 3-tab shingles (Josten Roofing 2026 NJ cost guide).
Architectural shingles commonly carry a 110-130 mph wind warranty versus roughly 60 mph (up to ~70 mph on entry products) for standard 3-tab shingles (manufacturer warranty language).

Architectural shingles are laminated, two-layer asphalt shingles built from a fiberglass mat saturated in asphalt and surfaced with mineral granules, bonding a second layer onto the base to create dimensional shadow lines (parent gold definition).

3-tab shingles are single-layer, flat-cut asphalt shingles built from a fiberglass mat saturated in asphalt and surfaced with mineral granules, with three cut tabs along each strip laying a flat uniform pattern (parent gold definition).
Architectural shingles weigh roughly 250-400+ lb per square versus 230-250 lb per square for 3-tab shingles (InterNACHI inspection guide).
Architectural shingles carry warranty ranges of 30-50 years versus 20-30 years for 3-tab shingles (InterNACHI asphalt-shingle inspection guide).

Architectural-grade Class 4 impact-resistant products pass a 2.0-inch steel ball dropped from 20 feet under UL 2218, the highest of four impact classes, with no crack through the shingle back after two strikes; standard 3-tab is typically unrated or low-class (UL 2218 standard).

Architectural shingles clear the IBC/IRC wind classification under ASTM D7158, whose Class F equivalent on the older ASTM D3161 fan test passes at 110 mph (NRCA Professional Roofing standards explainer).
Architectural failure modes are granule loss, zipper cracking along cutout lines, and cupping; 3-tab failure modes are tab curling, granule loss, and wind-uplift seal failure (parent gold).
Architectural single self-sealing-strip 3-tab loses protective granules under hail, exposing the asphalt mat and accelerating UV degradation (NRCA general guidance).
Laminated architectural shingles held roughly 57-58% of the asphalt-shingle market in 2024 (Mordor Intelligence).
Major asphalt-shingle makers including GAF, CertainTeed, and Owens Corning still produce 3-tab shingles, but as a declining minority of installs (parent gold FAQ).
InterNACHI notes that hail and high wind shorten asphalt-shingle life on either grade (InterNACHI life-expectancy chart).
Many homeowners insurers offer a premium credit for UL 2218 Class 4 roofs, set carrier by carrier (parent gold).
sources: NRCA (National Roofing Contractors Association) Professional Roofing standards explainer / general guidance
ASCE 7-16 (design wind speed, referenced by the NJ UCC)
IBC/IRC (International Building Code / International Residential Code)
Manufacturer warranty language (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning)
njContext: The NJ Uniform Construction Code treats a re-roof in architectural or 3-tab shingles as ordinary maintenance on a detached 1- or 2-family dwelling — no permit, inspection, or notice, regardless of shingle grade (N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7).

The NJ UCC requires a permit once roof work turns structural (replacing rafters, trusses, or ridge beams) or exceeds 25% of roof area within 12 months on commercial, condo, or attached buildings (N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7(b) and 5:23-2.7(c)), independent of shingle grade.

Essex County's mapped ASCE 7-16 design wind speed is ~110-115 mph; architectural's 110-130 mph warranty meets or exceeds it, while standard 3-tab at ~60 mph falls below it (ASCE 7-16 referenced by the NJ UCC, manufacturer warranty language).
Architectural shingles install at $6.50-$11.00 per NJ square foot and 3-tab at $5.50-$9.50 per NJ square foot (Josten Roofing 2026 NJ cost guide) — a per-square-foot gap, not a fixed dollar premium.

On a commercial steep-slope building, architectural or 3-tab roof work triggers a NJ UCC permit once it exceeds 25% of roof area in 12 months, since the ordinary-maintenance exemption covers only detached 1- and 2-family dwellings (N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7(c)).

Architectural shingles suit most owner-occupied Essex County houses (30-year life, 110-130 mph wind warranty); 3-tab suits budget-driven projects, rentals, and code-minimum re-roofs at the lower $5.50-$9.50 per NJ square-foot cost (InterNACHI and Josten Roofing).
positioning: Position Newark Quality Roofing as a registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor (N.J.S.A. 56:8-136 — NJ has no roofing license), insured, offering a free written estimate across Essex County. Frame the architectural-vs-3-tab recommendation on the verified evidence (InterNACHI lifespan, ASCE 7-16 Essex County design wind, UL 2218 impact class, Josten Roofing NJ cost) — not on field anecdote or storm-call counts. Warranty framing is honest and two-part: the manufacturer's material warranty plus NQR's written workmanship warranty; never cite or imply manufacturer certification tiers (no GAF Master Elite, no CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster). NQR installs both grades and matches the shingle to the building's use, budget, and northern-NJ wind exposure.
